name: Ivy creeper
description: A low strip of overlapping pointed ivy leaves on thin woody vines along the foot of a wall: flat and tall at the back where it hugs the wall, with a few runners climbing higher, spilling forward and down to the ground in front, uneven along its length and tapering off at both ends. Dark green inside, olive, and lit yellow-green on the top and rims; variants are a 1.5 m and a 0.8 m strip.

provenance.prompt: Ivy creeping along the foot of a wall: a low strip of overlapping ivy leaves on thin woody vines, about 1.5 m long (local x), about 0.25 m deep (y) and up to about 0.4 m high. A wall would stand behind it on +y, so the back side (+y) is flat and tall where it hugs the wall, with a few vine runners climbing higher on that back plane, and the leaves spill forward and down to the ground on -y. Uneven height along its length, ends tapering off so it blends into the ground. Two variants: ivy_creeper (1.5 m) and ivy_creeper_short (about 0.8 m). Leaves are small pointed leaf cards. Build each clump from many small leaf cards (thin bevel-free boxes about 4 mm thick, or strongly squashed subdiv=1 blobs) tilted at seeded angles around a darker core, in three greens: a deep shadow green inside and underneath, a mid olive green, and a lit yellow-green on the top and outer rims, so it reads dark inside, lit at the rims.
